title: Lesson 25. React — components, JSX, props
description: Components, JSX, differences from HTML, usage and props

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 25 — **React**. Before, all the page code was in one big file. React builds a page from small pieces — components, like a Lego set. Let's go!

slides.text: A **component** is an ordinary JS function that returns markup:
**JSX** is HTML right inside JS. The browser doesn't understand it itself; the build tool (Vite) converts it for us.

check.prompt: What is a component in React?
options: A JS function that returns markup
check.explain: A component is a piece of the page.

slides.text: In HTML it is `class="box"`, in JSX `className="box"`. In HTML ``, in JSX tags must be closed: ``.
This is the most common beginner mistake in React.

check.prompt: How do you set a class correctly in JSX?
check.explain: In JSX we write className instead of class.

slides.text: A component is used like an ordinary HTML tag:
**Props** are data from outside, like function parameters from lesson 16:
`{ title, price }` is destructuring from lesson 18.
Practice: a `Card` component with a title, text and an image, three cards. Homework: split the landing into `Header`, `Hero`, `Features`, `Footer`, each in its own file.

options: Data passed to a component from outside

questions.prompt: A React component is an ordinary JS function that returns markup.
Why does React split a page into components?
